title_en: Humanoid robots have beaten Usain Bolt's 100-meter dash record
title_fa: Humanoid robots have beaten Usain Bolt's 100-meter dash record
excerpt_en: And they looked absolutely ridiculous doing it.
excerpt_fa: و انجام آن کاملاً مضحک به نظر می رسیدند.
content_en:
Humanoid robots have beaten Usain Bolt's 100-meter dash record
And they looked absolutely ridiculous doing it.
Usain Bolt's 2009 world record for the 100-meter dash still remains unbroken at 9.58 seconds, but only if we're talking about humans. During the second annual World Humanoid Robot Games that kicked off in Beijing on Saturday, the Tiangong Ultra humanoid robot completed the 100-meter dash in 9.39 seconds during a preliminary heat. Developed by Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center, the record-holding robot overtook Honor's Lightning robot, which completed the sprint in 9.47 seconds.
Despite the impressive finish times, don't expect these humanoid robots to be used for any commercial purposes yet. After their sprints, they slammed directly into pads and some even required human assistance to be stretchered off the course. However, it's still a major improvement from last year's inaugural World Humanoid Robot Games, where the Tiangong Ultra won the 100-meter dash in 21.5 seconds.
Aside from this Robot Olympics event, Beijing hosted a half-marathon for Chinese companies to show off the capabilities of their humanoid robots. The event had its fair share of crashes too, but Honor's Lightning robot managed to secure the gold medal with a finish time of 50 minutes and 26 seconds, which also surpassed another human record. The World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing kicked off August 22 and will run until the 26, hosting thousands of robot participants competing in more than just track and field events, including soccer, table tennis and boxing.
content_fa:
روبات های انسان نما رکورد دوی 100 متر یوسین بولت را شکستند
و انجام آن کاملاً مضحک به نظر می رسیدند.
رکورد جهانی اوسین بولت در سال 2009 برای دوی 100 متر همچنان شکست ناپذیر باقی مانده است و 9.58 ثانیه است، اما فقط اگر در مورد انسان صحبت کنیم. در جریان دومین بازی سالانه جهانی ربات های انسان نما که از روز شنبه در پکن آغاز شد، ربات انسان نما Tiangong Ultra دوی 100 متر را در 9.39 ثانیه طی گرمای مقدماتی به پایان رساند. این ربات که توسط مرکز نوآوری ربات انسان نما پکن ساخته شده است، از ربات لایتنینگ آنر سبقت گرفت که این ربات اسپرینت را در 9.47 ثانیه به پایان رساند.
علیرغم زمان پایان قابل توجه، انتظار نداشته باشید که این روبات های انسان نما هنوز برای اهداف تجاری مورد استفاده قرار گیرند. پس از دوی سرعت، آنها مستقیماً به پدها برخورد کردند و حتی برخی از آنها نیاز به کمک انسانی داشتند تا از مسیر خارج شوند. با این حال، هنوز هم پیشرفت بزرگی نسبت به افتتاحیه بازی‌های ربات انسان‌نمای جهانی در سال گذشته است، جایی که Tiangong Ultra در 21.5 ثانیه دوی 100 متر را برد.
گذشته از این رویداد المپیک ربات، پکن میزبان یک نیمه ماراتن برای شرکت‌های چینی بود تا توانایی‌های روبات‌های انسان‌نما خود را به رخ بکشند. این رویداد سهم خود را در تصادفات نیز داشت، اما ربات لایتنینگ آنر توانست مدال طلا را با زمان پایان 50 دقیقه و 26 ثانیه به دست آورد که از یک رکورد انسانی دیگر نیز عبور کرد. بازی‌های جهانی ربات‌های انسان‌نما در پکن از 22 اوت آغاز شد و تا 26 آگوست ادامه خواهد داشت و میزبان هزاران شرکت‌کننده ربات است که در بیش از مسابقات دو و میدانی، از جمله فوتبال، تنیس روی میز و بوکس با هم رقابت می‌کنند.

title_en: Why are there so many fast charging standards, and what's the difference between them?
title_fa: Why are there so many fast charging standards, and what's the difference between them?
excerpt_en: A guide to the confusing world of USB-C fast charging.
excerpt_fa: A guide to the confusing world of USB-C fast charging.
content_en:
Why are there so many fast charging standards, and what's the difference between them?
A guide to the confusing world of USB-C fast charging.
"Fast charging" has become a catch-all term that can mean many different things. There's USB PD, PPS and even SuperVOOC, which sounds like a limit break in a Final Fantasy game. All the jargon for different standards can be confusing. Fortunately, there's less to worry about than that might suggest.
Years ago, USB charging was a slow trickle of power. But as mobile devices took over and demand for charging systems adapted accordingly, different companies developed their own approaches. That's how we ended up with Qualcomm's Quick Charge, Oppo's SuperVOOC and Xiaomi's HyperCharge — all proprietary systems advertising some form of fast charging.
To be clear, USB-C itself doesn't tell you much: A device with that port doesn't necessarily support fast charging. Many USB-C devices max out at slower speeds, and others use non-PD quick-charging methods. So, getting the fastest charge out of your phone is less about the port and more about what's going on inside.
Getting the absolute most out of fast charging usually means matching the device with the right cable and charger. Sadly, taking a phone that maxes out at 20W and plugging it into a 100W charger won't magically give you that full 100W. Likewise, if your phone supports a fast-charging protocol but your charger doesn't, you're out of luck. Here's what to look for instead.
The big standards
Today, USB Power Delivery (USB PD) is the closest we have to a universal standard. It's widely used across phones, tablets, laptops and some gaming portables.
Newer versions of USB PD push the standard forward. USB PD 3.1 raised the maximum supported power to 240W, while USB PD 3.2 is the spec's latest revision. Those higher power levels target demanding devices like laptops and monitors. Phones typically don't need anywhere near those maximum limits. Besides, thermal constraints would make 240W (or anything close to it) impractical and unnecessary for a handset anyway.
The iPhone 17 series is among the devices that support USB PD. Samsung and Google phones use fast-charging systems built around USB PD and its PPS feature.
PPS, or Programmable Power Supply, is one of the more advanced USB PD features available on phones. It lets the device request smaller, more precise voltage and current changes as it powers up. That can improve efficiency and help with heat management.
Samsung's Galaxy S26 Ultra uses PPS as part of its 60W "Super Fast Charging 3.0" system. Meanwhile, Google's Pixel 11 models use USB-C PPS charging to reach their fastest advertised speeds, with the Pixel 11 Pro designed for a 45W PPS charger. If you use Android flagships and want a versatile USB-C charger, PD with PPS is your go-to.
Remember Qualcomm Quick Charge? It was one of the first fast-charging systems for Android phones. Although it's still around, USB PD has become the more broadly adopted standard across the mobile industry, to the degree that even newer Quick Charge versions themselves support it. In fact, a Qualcomm chip doesn't even guarantee that the device uses Quick Charge, since phone makers can opt for other fast-charging systems instead.
Meanwhile, some Android phone makers use their own proprietary fast-charging systems. OnePlus and Oppo use technologies based on SuperVOOC, and Xiaomi uses HyperCharge on some models. The catch is that reaching the highest advertised speeds usually requires a compatible proprietary charger and, in many cases, the right cable, too. Still, many of these phones also support USB-C PD charging, although you might not get anywhere near the advertised speeds for the proprietary systems.
Speaking of which, it's good to take manufacturer claims with a few grains of salt anyway. Phones marketed as supporting 80W or 100W charging don't continuously draw that power from empty to full. Instead, they tend to charge fastest when the battery is fairly low, then rapidly taper the charging rate as the battery fills.
Fast charging and battery health
You may have heard that fast charging is bad for your battery, but that isn't necessarily the case. On one hand, lithium-ion batteries do degrade over time, and heat (which fast charging can generate more of) can indeed speed up that process. But today's phones are designed to manage that. They can monitor temperature, reduce power when it's called for and taper charging as the battery approaches full. So, don't worry too much about fast charging killing the battery's long-term health.
Still, remember that if you aren't in a hurry to have a full battery, there's also no long-term advantage to using fast charging. In other words, if all else is equal, a slower charge that keeps the temperature in check can be easier on the battery.
In practice, temperature management and charging habits have a bigger effect on battery longevity than the specific fast-charging protocol you use. So, avoid things like leaving your devices at a full charge all the time or charging an already hot phone in direct sunlight. You might also not want to steer clear of charging while playing games that push your phone to its limits. Some phones like the Galaxy S26 family have a setting that allows you to pause charging while gaming and use the current coming from your wall to power only the device. This maintains your battery level while not putting stress on the phone.
One of the best things you can do for your phone's battery is to use your phone's built-in battery-protection features. Apple's Optimized Battery Charging learns your habits and can delay charging past 80 percent when it expects the phone to stay plugged in for a while. iPhone 15 and newer models also let you customize the charge limit between 80 and 100 percent. Samsung and Google flagships have similar features: Battery Protection on Samsung phones, and Charging Optimization (including Adaptive Charging and an 80 percent limit)...
content_fa:
چرا استانداردهای شارژ سریع زیاد وجود دارد و تفاوت آنها چیست؟
راهنمای دنیای گیج کننده شارژ سریع USB-C.
"شارژ سریع" به یک اصطلاح فراگیر تبدیل شده است که می تواند معانی مختلفی داشته باشد. USB PD، PPS و حتی SuperVOOC وجود دارد که در بازی Final Fantasy مانند یک محدودیت به نظر می رسد. همه اصطلاحات برای استانداردهای مختلف می تواند گیج کننده باشد. خوشبختانه، نگرانی کمتری نسبت به آنچه ممکن است نشان دهد وجود دارد.
سال‌ها پیش، شارژ USB یک قطره آهسته قدرت بود. اما با تسلط بر دستگاه های تلفن همراه و تقاضا برای سیستم های شارژ متناسب با آن، شرکت های مختلف رویکردهای خود را توسعه دادند. اینگونه بود که به شارژ سریع Qualcomm، SuperVOOC Oppo و HyperCharge شیائومی رسیدیم - همه سیستم‌های اختصاصی که نوعی شارژ سریع را تبلیغ می‌کنند.
برای روشن بودن، USB-C خود چیز زیادی به شما نمی گوید: دستگاهی با آن پورت لزوماً از شارژ سریع پشتیبانی نمی کند. بسیاری از دستگاه‌های USB-C در سرعت‌های پایین‌تر به حداکثر می‌رسند و برخی دیگر از روش‌های شارژ سریع غیر PD استفاده می‌کنند. بنابراین، دریافت سریعترین شارژ از تلفن شما کمتر به پورت مربوط می شود و بیشتر به آنچه در داخل می گذرد مربوط می شود.
حداکثر استفاده از شارژ سریع معمولاً به معنای تطبیق دستگاه با کابل و شارژر مناسب است. متأسفانه، گرفتن یک تلفن با حداکثر توان 20 وات و وصل کردن آن به یک شارژر 100 واتی به طور جادویی آن 100 وات کامل را به شما نمی دهد. به همین ترتیب، اگر تلفن شما از پروتکل شارژ سریع پشتیبانی می کند اما شارژر شما از این پروتکل پشتیبانی نمی کند، شانس شما را ندارید. در اینجا چیزی است که باید به جای آن جستجو کنید.
استانداردهای بزرگ
امروزه، USB Power Delivery (USB PD) نزدیکترین چیزی است که ما به یک استاندارد جهانی داریم. این به طور گسترده در تلفن ها، تبلت ها، لپ تاپ ها و برخی از دستگاه های قابل حمل بازی استفاده می شود.
نسخه های جدیدتر USB PD استاندارد را به جلو می برند. USB PD 3.1 حداکثر توان پشتیبانی شده را به 240 وات افزایش داد، در حالی که USB PD 3.2 آخرین ویرایش مشخصات است. این سطوح قدرت بالاتر، دستگاه‌هایی مانند لپ‌تاپ و مانیتور را هدف قرار می‌دهند. تلفن ها معمولاً به جایی نزدیک به این حداکثر محدودیت ها نیاز ندارند. علاوه بر این، محدودیت های حرارتی 240 وات (یا هر چیزی نزدیک به آن) را برای یک گوشی غیرعملی و غیر ضروری می کند.
سری آیفون 17 از جمله دستگاه هایی است که از USB PD پشتیبانی می کند. گوشی‌های سامسونگ و گوگل از سیستم‌های شارژ سریع ساخته شده بر روی USB PD و ویژگی PPS آن استفاده می‌کنند.
PPS یا منبع تغذیه قابل برنامه ریزی یکی از پیشرفته ترین ویژگی های USB PD است که در تلفن ها موجود است. این به دستگاه اجازه می دهد تا هنگام روشن شدن، تغییرات ولتاژ و جریان کوچکتر و دقیق تری را درخواست کند. این می تواند کارایی را بهبود بخشد و به مدیریت گرما کمک کند.
گلکسی اس 26 اولترا سامسونگ از PPS به عنوان بخشی از سیستم شارژ سریع 3.0 60 واتی خود استفاده می کند. در همین حال، مدل‌های پیکسل 11 گوگل از شارژ USB-C PPS برای رسیدن به سریع‌ترین سرعت‌های تبلیغاتی خود استفاده می‌کنند، با Pixel 11 Pro که برای شارژر 45 واتی PPS طراحی شده است. اگر از پرچم‌داران اندرویدی استفاده می‌کنید و یک شارژر همه کاره USB-C می‌خواهید، PD با PPS بهترین گزینه است.
شارژ سریع کوالکام را به خاطر دارید؟ این یکی از اولین سیستم های شارژ سریع برای گوشی های اندرویدی بود. اگرچه هنوز هم وجود دارد، USB PD به استاندارد پذیرفته‌شده‌تر در صنعت موبایل تبدیل شده است، تا جایی که حتی نسخه‌های جدیدتر Quick Charge از آن پشتیبانی می‌کنند. در واقع، یک تراشه کوالکام حتی تضمین نمی کند که دستگاه از شارژ سریع استفاده می کند، زیرا سازندگان تلفن می توانند به جای آن سیستم های شارژ سریع دیگری را انتخاب کنند.
در همین حال، برخی از سازندگان تلفن های اندرویدی از سیستم های شارژ سریع اختصاصی خود استفاده می کنند. OnePlus و Oppo از فناوری‌های مبتنی بر SuperVOOC استفاده می‌کنند و شیائومی در برخی مدل‌ها از HyperCharge استفاده می‌کند. نکته مهم این است که دستیابی به بالاترین سرعت های تبلیغاتی معمولاً به یک شارژر اختصاصی سازگار و در بسیاری از موارد کابل مناسب نیز نیاز دارد. با این حال، بسیاری از این تلفن‌ها از شارژ USB-C PD نیز پشتیبانی می‌کنند، اگرچه ممکن است به سرعت‌های اعلام شده برای سیستم‌های اختصاصی نزدیک نشوید.
Speaking of which, it's good to take manufacturer claims with a few grains of salt anyway. Phones marketed as supporting 80W or 100W charging don't continuously draw that power from empty to full. Instead, they tend to charge fastest when the battery is fairly low, then rapidly taper the charging rate as the battery fills.
Fast charging and battery health
You may have heard that fast charging is bad for your battery, but that isn't necessarily the case. On one hand, lithium-ion batteries do degrade over time, and heat (which fast charging can generate more of) can indeed speed up that process. But today's phones are designed to manage that. They can monitor temperature, reduce power when it's called for and taper charging as the battery approaches full. So, don't worry too much about fast charging killing the battery's long-term health.
Still, remember that if you aren't in a hurry to have a full battery, there's also no long-term advantage to using fast charging. In other words, if all else is equal, a slower charge that keeps the temperature in check can be easier on the battery.
In practice, temperature management and charging habits have a bigger effect on battery longevity than the specific fast-charging protocol you use. So, avoid things like leaving your devices at a full charge all the time or charging an already hot phone in direct sunlight. You might also not want to steer clear of charging while playing games that push your phone to its limits. Some phones like the Galaxy S26 family have a setting that allows you to pause charging while gaming and use the current coming from your wall to power only the device. This maintains your battery level while not putting stress on the phone.
One of the best things you can do for your phone's battery is to use your phone's built-in battery-protection features. Apple's Optimized Battery Charging learns your habits and can delay charging past 80 percent when it expects the phone to stay plugged in for a while. iPhone 15 and newer models also let you customize the charge limit between 80 and 100 percent. Samsung and Google flagships have similar features: Battery Protection on Samsung phones, and Charging Optimization (including Adaptive Charging and an 80 percent limit)...

title_en: Does Analogue 3D really make retro games 4K? Here's what you should know
title_fa: آیا آنالوگ 3D واقعاً بازی های یکپارچهسازی با سیستمعامل را 4K می کند؟ در اینجا چیزی است که باید بدانید
excerpt_en: The Analogue 3D does a great job at upscaling old N64 games, with a few caveats.
excerpt_fa: Analogue 3D در ارتقای مقیاس بازی های قدیمی N64 با چند اخطار کار بسیار خوبی انجام می دهد.
content_en:
Does Analogue 3D really make retro games 4K? Here's what you should know
The Analogue 3D does a great job at upscaling old N64 games, with a few caveats.
Marketing is almost always a tad disingenuous, and Analogue's FPGA-based recreation of the Nintendo 64 is no exception. Words matter, and while the Analogue 3D does indeed output 4K video, it's not magically turning retro games into native 4K creations. The console's HDMI signal can reach 3,840 x 2,160 pixels on a compatible TV, while most original N64 games were rendered at significantly lower resolutions, commonly around 320 x 240, with some reaching 640 x 480.
In terms of literal output resolution, the Analogue 3D is a 4K console, but it's not capable of adding detailed textures, geometry or animation that developers couldn't cram into a mid-90s cartridge. A modern remake of Super Mario 64 would be quite different, though the Analogue 3D is pretty good at eliminating the N64's famously blurry textures, distance fog and uneven frame rates. The console also does far more than your basic upscaling, and what it does do definitely separates it from the pack.
What Analogue is presenting is a faithful, better-looking version of the original experience for those of us ready to jump into our mental time machines and head back to an era of landmark hardware and couch co-op. Its 4K HDMI output and customizable Original Display Modes are designed to make games look crisp and clear on today's TVs. While its not reinventing the wheel, its much more than a standard emulator.
What the Analogue 3D's 4k output really does
Analogue 3D utilizes a form of scaling, much like the upscaling smart TVs have used for years to fit lower-resolution video onto 4K panels. The difference here is that the Analogue 3D processes the N64's image before it reaches the TV. It can remove the original system's blur filter, preserve its 32-bit color, adjust texture filtering and anti-aliasing and (optionally) double a game's horizontal resolution. The console then outputs that processed image through a 4K HDMI signal.
If you're still pining for the vintage days of scanlines and the phosphor intensity of cathode ray displays, Analogue 3D can generate that vibe on a 65-inch, 4K screen. A stock N64 console connected to a modern TV through adapters tends to look blurry, blocky or weirdly processed, issues the Analogue 3D solves. The console also supports variable refresh rate, NTSC and PAL cartridges plus 1080p output alongside 4K.
It's all about the presentation, and a 4K output makes the signal cleaner and more stable for current TV displays. Of course, Analogue highly recommends using only a 4K display for the best experience, especially if you want to use Original Display Modes, which will only work on a 4K display.
Is the Analogue 3D worth buying for N64 games?
If you're holding onto some original N64 cartridges and want a much more polished means to play them on a 4k TV, the Analogue 3D is tough to beat at $250. It's designed for physical N64 media, works with the original controllers and accessories, is region-free and includes four controller ports. You also get Bluetooth and USB controller support. According to Analogue, it's compatible with every original N64 game, though its official hardware is not designed to support ROM files.
With that being said, accuracy and convenience are its biggest advantages. You won't find conventional software emulation here. The Analogue 3D uses an FPGA, a programmable chip that's configured to reproduce the N64's original operation, and Analogue does so without stepping on any trademark toes. It can also apply performance modes to certain games while avoiding the modern pitfalls of connecting an original N64 to a modern TV set.
If you're in the market for a link to the past (pun very much intended), the 3D is worth its weight in N64 gold. After all, it can capably turn your 30-year-old library of Nintendo 64 cartridges into a 4k gaming blast. Its 4k output, scaling and CRT-style display modes add that extra layer of nostalgia mixed with premium visuals on a modern display. For the right buyer, that's the entire point. It's a highly-rated, refined way to experience N64 games as they once were, without the controversy of another remake that ultimately redefines cherished memories of the past.
content_fa:
آیا آنالوگ 3D واقعاً بازی های یکپارچهسازی با سیستمعامل را 4K می کند؟ در اینجا چیزی است که باید بدانید
Analogue 3D در ارتقای مقیاس بازی های قدیمی N64 با چند اخطار کار بسیار خوبی انجام می دهد.
بازاریابی تقریباً همیشه کمی غیر صادقانه است، و بازسازی مبتنی بر FPGA آنالوگ از Nintendo 64 نیز از این قاعده مستثنی نیست. کلمات مهم هستند، و در حالی که Analogue 3D واقعاً ویدیوی 4K را تولید می کند، بازی های یکپارچهسازی با سیستمعامل را به طور جادویی به خلاقیت های 4K بومی تبدیل نمی کند. سیگنال HDMI کنسول می‌تواند روی یک تلویزیون سازگار به ۳۸۴۰ در ۲۱۶۰ پیکسل برسد، در حالی که اکثر بازی‌های اصلی N64 با وضوح بسیار پایین‌تری، معمولاً در حدود ۳۲۰ در ۲۴۰ و برخی به ۶۴۰ در ۴۸۰ می‌رسند.
از نظر وضوح خروجی واقعی، آنالوگ 3D یک کنسول 4K است، اما قادر به افزودن بافت‌ها، هندسه یا انیمیشن‌های دقیقی نیست که توسعه‌دهندگان نمی‌توانستند در یک کارتریج اواسط دهه 90 قرار دهند. بازسازی مدرن Super Mario 64 کاملاً متفاوت خواهد بود، اگرچه Analogue 3D در حذف بافت های تار معروف N64، مه فاصله و نرخ فریم ناهموار بسیار خوب است. کنسول همچنین بسیار بیشتر از ارتقاء اولیه شما انجام می دهد و کاری که انجام می دهد قطعاً آن را از بسته جدا می کند.
چیزی که آنالوگ ارائه می‌کند، نسخه‌ای وفادار و زیباتر از تجربه اصلی است که برای آن‌هایی از ما آماده است که به ماشین‌های زمان ذهنی خود بپریم و به عصر سخت‌افزار برجسته و کاناپه‌های تعاونی برگردیم. خروجی 4K HDMI و حالت‌های نمایش اصلی قابل تنظیم آن به گونه‌ای طراحی شده‌اند که بازی‌ها را در تلویزیون‌های امروزی واضح و شفاف نشان دهند. در حالی که چرخ را دوباره اختراع نمی کند، بسیار بیشتر از یک شبیه ساز استاندارد است.
آنچه که خروجی 4k آنالوگ 3D واقعا انجام می دهد
آنالوگ 3D از نوعی مقیاس‌بندی استفاده می‌کند، دقیقاً مانند تلویزیون‌های هوشمند ارتقاء دهنده که سال‌ها برای قرار دادن ویدیوهای با وضوح پایین‌تر بر روی پنل‌های 4K استفاده می‌کردند. تفاوت در اینجا این است که Analogue 3D تصویر N64 را قبل از رسیدن به تلویزیون پردازش می کند. این می‌تواند فیلتر تاری سیستم اصلی را حذف کند، رنگ 32 بیتی آن را حفظ کند، فیلتر بافت و ضد aliasing را تنظیم کند و (اختیاری) وضوح افقی بازی را دو برابر کند. سپس کنسول تصویر پردازش شده را از طریق یک سیگنال 4K HDMI خروجی می دهد.
اگر همچنان به روزهای قدیمی اسکن‌ها و شدت فسفر نمایشگرهای پرتو کاتدی پین می‌کنید، Analogue 3D می‌تواند آن حس را روی صفحه‌نمایش 65 اینچی و 4K ایجاد کند. کنسول N64 موجود که از طریق آداپتورها به یک تلویزیون مدرن متصل می‌شود، تار، مسدود یا به‌طور عجیبی پردازش شده به نظر می‌رسد، مشکلاتی که Analogue 3D حل می‌کند. این کنسول همچنین از نرخ نوسازی متغیر، کارتریج های NTSC و PAL به علاوه خروجی 1080p در کنار 4K پشتیبانی می کند.
همه چیز در مورد ارائه است و خروجی 4K سیگنال را برای نمایشگرهای تلویزیون فعلی تمیزتر و پایدارتر می کند. البته آنالوگ استفاده از نمایشگر 4K را برای بهترین تجربه به شدت توصیه می کند، به خصوص اگر می خواهید از حالت های نمایش اصلی استفاده کنید که فقط روی صفحه نمایش 4K کار می کند.
آیا Analogue 3D ارزش خرید برای بازی های N64 را دارد؟
اگر چند کارتریج اصلی N64 را در دست دارید و می‌خواهید ابزار بسیار صیقلی‌تری برای پخش آن‌ها در تلویزیون 4k داشته باشید، آنالوگ 3D با قیمت 250 دلار سخت است. این برای رسانه های فیزیکی N64 طراحی شده است، با کنترلرها و لوازم جانبی اصلی کار می کند، بدون منطقه است و شامل چهار پورت کنترلر است. همچنین از بلوتوث و کنترلر USB پشتیبانی می کنید. به گفته آنالوگ، با هر بازی اصلی N64 سازگار است، اگرچه سخت افزار رسمی آن برای پشتیبانی از فایل های ROM طراحی نشده است.
با توجه به آنچه گفته شد، دقت و راحتی بزرگترین مزیت آن است. در اینجا شبیه سازی نرم افزار معمولی را نخواهید یافت. Analogue 3D از FPGA استفاده می کند، یک تراشه قابل برنامه ریزی که برای بازتولید عملکرد اصلی N64 پیکربندی شده است، و Analogue این کار را بدون پا گذاشتن روی هیچ علامت تجاری انجام می دهد. همچنین می‌تواند حالت‌های عملکردی را برای بازی‌های خاص اعمال کند و در عین حال از مشکلات مدرن اتصال N64 اصلی به تلویزیون مدرن اجتناب کند.
اگر به دنبال پیوندی به گذشته هستید (جناسی که در نظر گرفته شده است)، 3D ارزش وزن خود را در طلای N64 دارد. به هر حال، می‌تواند کتابخانه 30 ساله کارتریج‌های نینتندو 64 شما را به یک انفجار بازی 4k تبدیل کند. خروجی 4k، مقیاس‌بندی و حالت‌های نمایشگر به سبک CRT، این لایه نوستالژی اضافی را با جلوه‌های بصری ممتاز در یک نمایشگر مدرن اضافه می‌کند. برای خریدار مناسب، این تمام نکته است. این روشی با امتیاز بالا و تصفیه شده برای تجربه بازی‌های N64 مانند گذشته است، بدون بحث در مورد بازسازی دیگری که در نهایت خاطرات ارزشمند گذشته را بازتعریف می‌کند.

title_en: Twitch and Amazon hit with lawsuit for training AI with streamers' content
title_fa: Twitch and Amazon hit with lawsuit for training AI with streamers' content
excerpt_en: The class action suit claims that Amazon never obtained consent from Twitch streamers to be used to train its AI models.
excerpt_fa: The class action suit claims that Amazon never obtained consent from Twitch streamers to be used to train its AI models.
content_en:
Twitch and Amazon hit with lawsuit for training AI with streamers' content
The class action suit claims that Amazon never obtained consent from Twitch streamers to be used to train its AI models.
A streamer has taken a stand against Twitch and Amazon using his content to train AI models. Warren Pandiscia, a streamer based in Connecticut, filed a class action lawsuit earlier this week, as first reported by Courthouse News. The complaint accused Twitch and Amazon of not obtaining licensing or permission before using his Twitch streams and videos as a "dataset necessary to fuel Amazon's AI products."
Earlier this month, Twitch Support posted on X that it added an option to opt out of "having your channel content used to train generative AI content models across Amazon." Shortly after, Twitch hosted an episode of its recurring Patch Notes stream where Mike Minton, the company's chief product officer, said "if it was opt-in, nobody would opt in," when asked by a viewer why the Twitch settings for AI training aren't opt-in but instead enabled by default, requiring users to opt out if they don't want to participate.
Now, the latest class action lawsuit claims that Twitch and Amazon committed a breach of contract when the companies decided to use its streamers as "free training stock for separate commercial AI products." The complaint also accused the two companies of benefitting from their streamers, who "lost money or property as a result of defendants' unlawful, unfair and fraudulent practices."
Amazon isn't the only company that's been hit with a lawsuit for allegedly using content creators for AI training. Earlier this year, three YouTubers filed a class action lawsuit against Apple, accusing the company of scraping copyrighted content to train its AI models.

Amazon isn't the only company that's been hit with a lawsuit for allegedly using content creators for AI training. Earlier this year, three YouTubers filed a class action lawsuit against Apple, accusing the company of scraping copyrighted content to train its AI models.

title_en: Is it safe to use a USB-C laptop charger on your phone?
title_fa: Is it safe to use a USB-C laptop charger on your phone?
excerpt_en: If you've ever wondered whether you can just charge your phone with the cable for your laptop, read on and find out how to tell.
excerpt_fa: If you've ever wondered whether you can just charge your phone with the cable for your laptop, read on and find out how to tell.
content_en:
Is it safe to use a USB-C laptop charger on your phone?
Or will using the wrong cable fry your phone?
It's a common occurrence: You have your fully charged laptop plugged in before you, but your smartphone is seriously lagging behind. So, you unplug the charger from your laptop and use it with your phone. Both have USB-C ports, so it should be OK, right? That's the big question that we've all asked ourselves, especially as USB-C is now common across phones, tablets and laptops. It's easy to assume every charger works the same way, and, in practice, it's a safe bet to make. Modern charging standards are designed to make it possible to mix and match your chargers and devices safely.
Something you should know is that a USB-C laptop charger does not simply force maximum wattage into a phone. In fact, modern USB-C charging is governed by the USB Power Delivery standard, which is a protocol that enables a charger and a device to communicate before any significant power is transferred.
That said, just because using a high-power charger is considered to be generally safe doesn't mean there aren't situations that come with a risk. Charging results can vary depending on the charger, cable, phone model and charging protocol involved. A high-quality USB-C laptop charger from a reputable manufacturer is usually fine for a modern smartphone, but older devices, cheap accessories and damaged cables can still create issues.
How does USB power delivery actually work?
USB Power Delivery (USB-PD) is a charging standard developed by the USB Implementers Forum (USB-IF) that governs how power flows between a charger and a device. The key thing to remember here is that it's not the charger pushing power into your phone, but rather the phone pulling exactly what it needs.
When you plug in a device, there's a back-and-forth happening. The charger will transmit its full range of power levels to the smartphone, and the smartphone will accept the highest level it can safely use from the list. Because of this negotiation process, a high-wattage charger cannot fry your phone's circuits. The phone will never actually absorb more power than its internal components are designed to handle.
When is it safe to use a laptop charger on your phone?
In short? Almost always, provided both devices were made in the last decade or so. All recent iPhones, Pixel phones, Galaxy devices, MacBooks and most Windows laptops these days support USB-PD. When both your charger and phone are USB-PD compatible, the negotiation process described above kicks in automatically and you can use that combination every day without issue.
So what happens if one or both devices lack USB-PD support? It's still generally fine because a USB-PD charger connected to a non-USB-PD phone will simply default to a safe output. Even if the negotiation steps are skipped, the phone will charge slowly but safely. Similarly, a non-USB-PD charger connected to a USB-PD phone will cap out at 5V/3A, which is more than enough for a slow, safe charge.
Will a laptop charger charge your phone faster?
The answer to this question really depends on your phone's fast-charging capabilities. If your phone supports higher-voltage charging and the laptop charger can deliver it, then yes, you'll likely see faster charging speeds than with a standard wall adapter. For example, Apple states that fast charging for many recent iPhones requires a compatible 20W or higher USB-C power adapter. A 65W laptop charger clears that bar quite easily, so your iPhone will negotiate the power it needs and charge accordingly. You should also be aware that some smartphone brands use their own proprietary charging protocols that require their specific cable or power brick to achieve advertised speeds.
However, if your phone is limited to 18W or 20W input, plugging it into a 100W laptop charger won't make it charge any faster, as the phone will only pull what it's rated for. More watts on the charger label doesn't mean more speed; it just means the charger has headroom for other devices. Since you'll most often see 100W, 140W or higher on multi-port chargers, those maximum outputs are designed to "cover" all plugged-in devices. The reverse, namely using your phone's charger with your laptop, won't deliver the same quick charge you are used to achieving. Oh, and you shouldn't expect impressive results if you use your car's USB ports to charge your laptop, either.
You should still exercise caution when charging your devices, especially if you have cheap, uncertified chargers. Counterfeit or poorly engineered chargers often bypass essential isolation barriers between the AC mains and the DC output side, so a surge in that type of device can pass damaging voltage spikes to your phone. Low-quality cables are also a hidden risk, as a non-certified USB-C cable may lack the internal pull-up resistor required by the USB-C spec. As a rule of thumb, before you use any charger, check it for safety certification markings such as Underwriters Laboratories (UL), Intertek (ETL) or the CE mark.
Since we've focused on whether or not it's a good idea to charge your smartphone with your laptop brick, you should know that other smaller USB-C devices may not come with the same microcontrollers needed to properly communicate with a high-power charger. Most fast chargers start at 5V and only step up after negotiation, so the risk is usually low, but you should still stick to the charger that came in the box, just in case.

title_en: Is a liquid-cooled PC worth it?
title_fa: Is a liquid-cooled PC worth it?
excerpt_en: Air cooling is reliable, while liquid cooling is visually slick. Which one you should use depends on how heavy you game on your system.
excerpt_fa: Air cooling is reliable, while liquid cooling is visually slick. Which one you should use depends on how heavy you game on your system.
content_en:
Is a liquid-cooled PC worth it?
Liquid-cooled systems look amazing, but come at a cost premium compared to air coolers.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
A liquid cooling system can be one of the star components of a custom-built gaming PC, but are they really worth the money? After all, they're usually a lot more expensive than traditional air coolers. AIO (all-in-one) liquid cooling systems often look flashy and can sometimes be tricky to install, but there's a reason they're all the rage with high-end PC builders.
Let's get into how liquid coolers work, the main differences between them and traditional heatsink models, and when it makes sense to opt for an AIO system over a tried-and-true air cooler.
Liquid CPU coolers vs. air coolers: The key differences
At their core, both liquid and air coolers perform the same function: they move heat away from a PC's CPU. Where they differ is in the methods used to transfer the heat. Air coolers use a heatsink and pipes to regulate a processor's temperature, whereas liquid systems use coolant. Air coolers are generally simpler in their makeup than AIO models, consisting of only a cold plate, pipes, a fan and a heatsink. Liquid coolers are a little more complicated, being composed of a plate, pump, tubing, coolant, a separate radiator and accompanying fans.
Liquid coolers are typically aimed at a different market than their air alternatives. AIO systems are good for high-end gaming PCs where 4K output at console-beating frame rates is the priority. Aiming for 120FPS gameplay in Ultra HD puts a lot of load on the CPU. To prevent overheating and thermal throttling, a liquid cooler with a large radiator dissipates heat more effectively than an air cooler. On the flipside, while air coolers aren't as well-suited for top-of-the-line gaming processors, they're ideal for budget or mid-range PCs where the CPU is less likely to be under constant heavy load.
How do liquid CPU coolers work?
A liquid cooler regulates the heat of a CPU by directing heat away from the processor via a water block, cooling pump and a radiator. When you install a CPU for the first time, you apply thermal paste to the top of the chip to help the cooler transfer heat more effectively. Once the paste has absorbed heat, it's passed onto the water block's copper plate, whereby the heat is transferred into liquid.
After this step, the cooler's pump directs this liquid towards the radiator, which is most commonly installed above a PC's motherboard. Once the liquid reaches the radiator, the heat from the coolant is dissipated by its fans, and the newly cooled liquid is then sent back to the water block in a cycle that constantly repeats whenever your PC is running.
Custom loop cooling systems work a little differently. Unlike an AIO unit where all the components come in the box, custom loops let you choose every part of the cooler (including the water block, radiator, tubing, fans and reservoir. The reservoir is what stores the system's coolant while also feeding the pump. If you like, you can also set up custom loops to cool more than just the CPU. With the right tweaks, you can integrate a GPU water block into a custom loop system to help regulate the temperature of your graphics card.
Should I go with a liquid cooler or an air cooler?
If you own one of the top gaming CPUs, like the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, you should definitely go with a liquid cooler. I've had the aforementioned processor for a couple of years, and I'm glad I decided to pair it with the NZXT Kraken 360. This high-end 360mm AIO cooler offers comprehensive customization via the NZXT CAM app, allowing me to set precise performance targets while also providing an abundance of RGB lighting options.
The added thermal headroom a liquid cooler grants my custom-built PC allows me to run the best and most demanding PC titles at 4K/120FPS without ever having to worry about overheating. Top-tier liquid coolers like the Kraken 360 can also run at whisper-quiet levels, and they look so much sharper than the fan alternative. It's worth noting that cheaper liquid coolers can get a little noisy. In general, models with larger 280 and 360mm radiators can dissipate substantially more heat compared to air coolers, making them the go-to choice for cutting-edge PC builds.
Of course, there are downsides to going with a liquid cooler, though none of them should be considered deal-breakers. High-end models can cost upwards of $200, which is way more expensive than even the best air coolers. AIO models are also trickier to install, as you're not just dealing with the pump; you also need to secure the radiator inside your case. Maintenance is another issue. Whereas air coolers need very little tinkering after being installed, the pump of a liquid cooler will wear over time. There's also the (fairly low) possibility of leakage, which could damage other components inside your PC if it does occur.
Moving onto air coolers, they're the best bet for all but the most hardcore of PC players. Unless you're rocking a rig with an Intel Core i9-14900K and a Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 (our review), you probably don't need a liquid cooler. If you're a casual Steam user with a mid-range system that houses a relatively modest CPU, an air cooler will work just fine. As they're cheaper, easier to install and have generally longer lifespans than AIO models, they're the ideal processor-cooling solution for folks who aren't obsessed with aesthetics. As long as you don't mind staring at a big heatsink if you have a case with a transparent window, air coolers are the most sensible option for the majority of PC gamers.

title_en: TechCrunch Mobility: The custom chip driving Waymo’s robotaxi ambitions
title_fa: TechCrunch Mobility: The custom chip driving Waymo’s robotaxi ambitions
excerpt_en: Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility — your central hub for news and insights on the future of transportation.
excerpt_fa: Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility — your central hub for news and insights on the future of transportation.
content_en:
Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility — your central hub for news and insights on the future of transportation. To get this in your inbox, sign up here for free — just click TechCrunch Mobility!
Waymo gets a lot of attention for its fast-paced expansion. And for good reason; it seems like every week, the company’s robotaxis are arriving in a new city, or expanding within an existing service area.
We’ve known for a while that Waymo’s sixth-generation self-driving system — which debuted in its next-generation Ojai robotaxi — is central to those ambitions. But now we have a better understanding about why.
The company, which just opened its Ojai robotaxi to all riders in Los Angeles, Phoenix, and San Francisco, has repeatedly said that this next-gen vehicle is cheaper to build, operate, and maintain — ingredients required if the company has any hopes of someday turning a profit.
What was less clear, until this week, was just how hands-on and vertically integrated Waymo has become as it chases that goal.
The company shared this week that it built a custom silicon chip — specifically a 5 nm ASIC chip, which is designed to handle the massive influx of raw data before it reaches the core “brain” of the self-driving system. (To get a sense of how much data, consider that the Waymo Ojai has 13 high-fidelity cameras.) Waymo said the chip delivers more than 1,000 TOPS (trillions of operations per second) of computing performance, a statistic that puts it roughly in the same performance range as Nvidia’s latest DRIVE AGX Thor automotive processor, a powerful computer designed for automated driving applications.
The end result, Waymo says, is a system that has “unmatched efficiency and performance.” The upshot: Waymo contends that this chip is a critical piece of a system that can react fast and safely in complex, high-density environments — like cities.
It’s worth noting that Waymo isn’t working alone on compute. The company listed a slew of partners, some for the first time, that includes AMD, Micron, Nvidia, Samsung, Sandisk, Socionext, and TSMC.
A little bird
A couple of little birds spoke to Sean O’Kane (senior reporter, special projects at TechCrunch) about a rather curious investigation being conducted by the Idaho National Laboratory.
According to our sources, the lab is evaluating whether Chinese lidar sensors might pose a security risk if they become widely used on vehicles in the United States. That is notable on its own. But what got our attention is that the research is being funded by a company — or a group of companies — in the electric and autonomous vehicle industries.
O’Kane reached out to numerous companies, including Rivian, General Motors, Ford, Kodiak, Lucid Motors, Nuro, and Uber. And all of these companies said they were unaware of the review. Aurora, Nvidia, and Zoox didn’t respond to questions.
Got a tip for us? Email Kirsten Korosec at kirsten.korosec@techcrunch.com or my Signal at kkorosec.07, or email Sean O’Kane at sean.okane@techcrunch.com.
Deals!
Also, the startup incubated within Rivian, has raised another $150 million in a Series D round led by Prysm Capital with participation from existing backers Eclipse, Greenoaks, and MVP Ventures. Also has raised $455 million since it spun out of Rivian in March 2025.
The raise is notable, and not just because Also has already reached a Series D round after launching just a little more than a year ago. The company’s mission has also evolved, which helps explain why it still needs to keep raising cash.
When Also launched in spring 2025, it was described as a micromobility company focused on pedal-assist electric bikes and commercial cargo quads. Now it is a “Palo Alto-based technology company building the world’s most capable driven and autonomous small electric vehicles.”
That autonomous driving component popped up earlier this year when Also closed a $200 million round and announced a multiyear commercial agreement with DoorDash to develop and deploy autonomous delivery vehicles.
Sidewalk delivery robot company Serve Robotics also had a notable and very timely deal this week. You might recall that earlier this month, Serve reported during its earning call that Uber had reduced its use of its robots on the app; that partnership is set to end next year. Separately, Uber also sold all of its shares in the company.
Months before these changes, Serve was working on several other deals that were recently finalized, according to insiders. Serve has partnered with Grubhub to use its sidewalk robots, starting in Chicago, Los Angeles, and Alexandria, Virginia. Serve also announced that its existing partnership with DoorDash has expanded to San Jose, California, and Washington, D.C.
Uber’s retreat from Serve illustrates an important lesson for any company attempting to scale: Always diversify. And it seems Serve has managed to do that.
Other deals that got my attention …
Einride, the Swedish electric and autonomous trucking company, struck a deal with Tesla to buy 500 of its electric Semis and make the electric big rigs available to its customers, which include Amazon. The Tesla Semis will be added in phases to Einride’s fleet over the next 24 months, starting in September. Reminder: Tesla is trying to scale up but recently pulled back on promises to reach “volume production” in 2026.
Grounded, the Detroit-based startup that customizes electric and gas-powered vans, raised a $5 million seed round, with repeat investments from existing backers Also Capital and Chicago-based early-stage firm The 81 Collection, along with Animal Capital, the Michigan Outdoor Innovation Fund, and “various SpaceX alumni,” according to founder and CEO Sam Shapiro.
Uber said it is investing in, and partnering with, drone delivery company Zipline. Uber and Zipline didn’t disclose the investment amount but did share one lofty goal: to make 1 million deliveries per day using the startup’s drones by the end of 2029.

title_en: Flock CEO calls for ‘compromise’ as surveillance company faces growing backlash
title_fa: Flock CEO calls for ‘compromise’ as surveillance company faces growing backlash
excerpt_en: Flock Safety faces a growing public outcry over concerns that its surveillance technology could be misused.
excerpt_fa: Flock Safety faces a growing public outcry over concerns that its surveillance technology could be misused.
content_en:
The country needs to find a “compromise” between privacy and safety, according to Flock Safety CEO Garrett Langley.
“When people talk about just one of these, privacy or safety, they’re prioritizing the wrong thing, and what we have to prioritize as a country is compromise,” Langley said during a recent interview with Fox News. “How do we have our safety, and how do we balance privacy?”
Langley’s Fox News appearance was just the latest interview he’s given as the company faces a growing public outcry around concerns that Flock’s surveillance cameras, drones, and license plate recognition technology could be misused.
These concerns aren’t just hypothetical. The Washington Post recently identified 46 cases where police officers have been accused of using Flock technology for unauthorized purposes, including to stalk their wives, girlfriends, or exes.
After listening to an interview with one of the alleged victims, Langley told CBS News, “I apologize. It kills me that she went through that.” At the same time, he insisted, “I don’t think that Flock created police abuse. I think we’re the first company to ever shine a light on it and build the tools to find it.”
Just as the data center backlash has become a potent issue on both the left and the right, both Democratic and Republican politicians have begun to take aim at Flock.
On the left, Michigan’s Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed recently accused his opponent Mike Rogers of supporting “this mass proliferation of Flock cameras, any and everywhere, watching your every move to collect information without you even noticing.” And Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders posted, “STOP AI MASS SURVEILLANCE. STOP FLOCK.”
On the right, three House Republicans recently introduced a bill that would prohibit the federal government from purchasing automated surveillance systems that use facial recognition, biometric IDs, or license plate recognition, “including a Flock Safety camera.”
Flock has already made some changes in response to the criticism, reducing the default data retention time from 30 days to seven days and requiring that a case code be entered before accessing data. But both of these changes can be overridden — for example, police can save data for a longer time period by using a setting called Evidence Mode.
In its response to Flock’s announced changes, the American CIvil Liberties Union said, “While Flock has not shortened the default retention period to the ACLU’s recommended 48 hours, its proposal may be a step in the right direction. Whether this is a real change or just another Flock PR move, however, will depend on how its ‘Evidence Mode’ operates.”
For his part, Langley has said that state regulators should “pass bills that make [the illegal use of Flock data] a criminal offense.” And during his Fox News interview, he pointed to the changes the company has already made, while also saying, “Today, it is too often that in Flock and in other technologies, there’s no regulation. There’s no accountability, and we think that’s wrong.”
TechCrunch will also be asking Langley about these issues when he appears on-stage at our Disrupt conference in October.
content_fa:
به گفته گرت لنگلی، مدیر عامل Flock Safety، این کشور باید بین حریم خصوصی و ایمنی "سازش" پیدا کند.
لنگلی در مصاحبه اخیر خود با فاکس نیوز گفت: «وقتی مردم فقط در مورد یکی از این موارد صحبت می‌کنند، حریم خصوصی یا ایمنی، چیز اشتباه را در اولویت قرار می‌دهند، و چیزی که ما به عنوان یک کشور باید در اولویت قرار دهیم، مصالحه است. "چگونه امنیت خود را داریم و چگونه حریم خصوصی را متعادل می کنیم؟"
حضور لنگلی در فاکس نیوز تنها آخرین مصاحبه ای بود که وی انجام داد، زیرا این شرکت با اعتراض مردمی فزاینده در مورد نگرانی هایی که از دوربین های نظارتی، پهپادها و فناوری تشخیص پلاک Flock ممکن است سوء استفاده شود، مواجه است.
این نگرانی ها فقط فرضی نیستند. واشنگتن پست اخیراً 46 مورد را شناسایی کرده است که در آن افسران پلیس متهم به استفاده از فناوری Flock برای مقاصد غیرمجاز از جمله تعقیب همسران، دوست دختران یا سابق خود شده اند.
لنگلی پس از گوش دادن به مصاحبه با یکی از قربانیان ادعایی، به CBS News گفت: "من عذرخواهی می‌کنم. این مرا می‌کشد که او این کار را انجام داده است." در همان زمان، او اصرار داشت: "فکر نمی‌کنم که Flock باعث سوء استفاده پلیس شده باشد. فکر می‌کنم ما اولین شرکتی هستیم که تا به حال به آن نور می‌تابانیم و ابزارهایی برای یافتن آن می‌سازیم."
همانطور که واکنش متقابل مرکز داده ها به یک موضوع مهم در چپ و راست تبدیل شده است، سیاستمداران دموکرات و جمهوری خواه هر دو شروع به هدف قرار دادن Flock کرده اند.
در سمت چپ، عبدالالسید، نامزد دموکرات سنای میشیگان، اخیراً رقیب خود مایک راجرز را متهم کرد که از «تکثیر انبوه دوربین‌های Flock، در هر کجا و در همه جا، تماشای هر حرکت شما برای جمع‌آوری اطلاعات بدون اینکه حتی متوجه شوید، حمایت می‌کند». و برنی سندرز، سناتور ایالت ورمونت، پستی را منتشر کرد: " نظارت انبوه هوش مصنوعی را متوقف کنید.
در سمت راست، سه جمهوری‌خواه مجلس نمایندگان اخیراً لایحه‌ای ارائه کردند که دولت فدرال را از خرید سیستم‌های نظارت خودکار که از تشخیص چهره، شناسه‌های بیومتریک یا تشخیص پلاک استفاده می‌کنند، «از جمله دوربین ایمنی گله» منع می‌کند.
Flock قبلاً تغییراتی را در پاسخ به انتقادات اعمال کرده است و زمان پیش‌فرض نگهداری داده‌ها را از 30 روز به 7 روز کاهش داده و قبل از دسترسی به داده‌ها باید کد موردی وارد شود. اما هر دوی این تغییرات را می توان نادیده گرفت – برای مثال، پلیس می تواند با استفاده از تنظیماتی به نام حالت شواهد، داده ها را برای مدت زمان طولانی تری ذخیره کند.
اتحادیه آزادی های مدنی آمریکا در پاسخ به تغییرات اعلام شده Flock گفت: "در حالی که Flock دوره نگهداری پیش فرض را به 48 ساعت توصیه شده ACLU کوتاه نکرده است، پیشنهاد آن ممکن است گامی در جهت درست باشد. با این حال، این که آیا این یک تغییر واقعی است یا فقط یک اقدام دیگر Flock PR، به نحوه عملکرد "حالت شواهد" آن بستگی دارد.
به نوبه خود، لنگلی گفته است که تنظیم‌کننده‌های ایالتی باید «لایحه‌هایی را تصویب کنند که [استفاده غیرقانونی از داده‌های Flock] را به عنوان یک جرم مجرمانه تبدیل کند». و در طول مصاحبه خود با فاکس نیوز، او به تغییراتی که شرکت قبلاً ایجاد کرده است اشاره کرد، در حالی که همچنین گفت: "امروز، اغلب اوقات در Flock و سایر فناوری‌ها، هیچ مقرراتی وجود ندارد. هیچ پاسخگویی وجود ندارد، و ما فکر می‌کنیم این اشتباه است."
TechCrunch همچنین وقتی لنگلی در کنفرانس Disrupt ما در اکتبر روی صحنه ظاهر می شود، درباره این مسائل می پرسد.

title_en: These modern smartwatches are in their last year of updates
title_fa: These modern smartwatches are in their last year of updates
excerpt_en: A whole bunch of smart watches are getting phased out this year. Is your watch on the list?
excerpt_fa: A whole bunch of smart watches are getting phased out this year. Is your watch on the list?
content_en:
These modern smartwatches are in their last year of updates
It might be time for an upgrade.
There are several popular smartwatches that are going to reach end-of-life in 2026, from the Pixel Watch 2 to Samsung's Galaxy Watch 5 and 5 Pro, as well as a whole slew of Apple Watch models. These devices won't stop working, but they'll stop receiving new features and, in some cases, security patches.
A lot can change in three years. The smartwatch on your wrist may have felt cutting-edge when you first strapped it on, but for a growing number of popular models, 2026 marks the final year of guaranteed software support. That's true among all three major platforms: Apple, Google and Samsung.
What does that actually mean? Your older watch model won't suddenly stop working, but it will stop moving forward. They'll work just fine tracking steps and delivering notifications, but if you're using the watch for contactless payments or storing sensitive health data, the lack of ongoing security updates should fire up some alarms.
It's also worth noting the scale of this year's changes. Apple alone is dropping five models with a single watchOS update — an absolutely massive cut. Add in Google's three-year support window expiring and Samsung's Wear OS cutoffs for the Watch 5 lineup, and 2026 shapes up as a significant moment for smartwatch owners to take stock of where their device stands.
Which Apple Watch models are losing support in 2026?
Right now, the latest models from Apple are Watch Series 11, Ultra 3 and the budget-friendly Watch SE (3rd generation). The only Apple Watch models compatible with watchOS 27 are Apple Watch Series 9, Apple Watch Series 10, Apple Watch Series 11, Apple Watch Ultra 2 and Ultra 3, and Apple Watch SE (3rd generation).
That means that, with the upcoming release of watchOS 27, the Apple Watch Series 6, Series 7, Series 8, Apple Watch SE 2nd gen and the first-generation Apple Watch Ultra will no longer be supported. This seems to be a hardware-related situation where modern Siri works best with the chips inside Apple Watch Series 9 and up. Apple usually gives Watch models between three and six years of major OS support before being phased out, and the Series 8 and Ultra (1st gen) both released in 2022.
The release of watchOS 27 is expected to happen sometime in mid-September 2026. Apple usually releases major watchOS updates around the same time new iPhone and Apple Watch hardware launches in September. WatchOS 27 was initially announced in June and went through developer and public beta testing over the summer.
Is the Google Pixel Watch 2 losing support in 2026?
According to Google's official support page, the Pixel Watch 2, which was released in October 2023, has a guaranteed software update window running until October 1, 2026. That includes both Wear OS version updates and security patches. Once that date passes — and we're not that far from it — the Pixel Watch 2 will no longer receive either.
Google's current Pixel Watch lineup follows a clear three-year support policy from the device's release date on the Google Store. Therefore, here's when to expect end-of-life for your device:
-
Pixel Watch 2: October 2026
-
Pixel Watch 3: October 2027
-
Pixel Watch 4: October 2028
Google offers an industry-leading seven years of support for its Pixel smartphones, but has yet to apply a similar policy for the Pixel Watch lineup. At this point, Google offers the shortest watch support lifespan out of the major brands.
Which Samsung Galaxy Watch models are nearing the end of Wear OS upgrades?
Samsung's own approach to support is a bit different, splitting its commitment into two tiers. First of all, you get one timeline for Wear OS upgrades and another for security updates. In recent years, Samsung has offered four major OS upgrades and five years of security patches per device.
Here's the timeline for Samsung's models:
-
Galaxy Watch 4 and Watch 4 Classic (August 2021): Wear OS support already ended; security upgrades will stop in the near future.
-
Galaxy Watch 5 and Watch 5 Pro (August 2022): will get Wear OS upgrades until December 31, 2026; security upgrades continue.
-
Galaxy Watch 6 and Watch 6 Classic (August 2023): will get Wear OS upgrades until December 2027; security upgrades continue.
-
Galaxy Watch FE: will get Wear OS upgrades until December 2028; security upgrades continue.
What happens when a smartwatch loses support?
The words "end of support" sound a bit more alarming than they should be. The end of the world is not approaching, you do not need to immediately get an upgrade and you won't be left with a brick on your wrist. Your watch won't suddenly stop working, and you'll still be able to track your workouts, get notifications and use most of the features you rely on daily.
What you lose is forward momentum. There will be no OS features, no app compatibility improvements and potentially no security patches, depending on the manufacturer. This can be quite risky if you use your watch for payments, for instance, as a lack of patched vulnerabilities might allow hackers room to exploit payment data. The same happens with these massively popular smartphones that are in their last year of software support.
As 2026 is a major checkpoint for smartwatch owners across major platforms, it might be time to look into an upgrade.

title_en: Is it legal to train AI models on copyrighted books? It’s complicated
title_fa: آیا آموزش مدل های هوش مصنوعی بر روی کتاب های دارای حق چاپ قانونی است؟ پیچیده است
excerpt_en: Most published authors have, without their knowledge or consent, contributed to the development of the same AI tools that threaten to undermine their livelihoods. That seems illegal, right?
excerpt_fa: Most published authors have, without their knowledge or consent, contributed to the development of the same AI tools that threaten to undermine their livelihoods. That seems illegal, right?
content_en:
You probably know by now that the AI models powering ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and other chatbots are trained on seemingly infinite databases of published works, containing hundreds of millions of books, online articles, academic papers, and basically anything you can find on the internet. Most published authors have, without their knowledge or consent, contributed to the development of the same AI tools that threaten to undermine their livelihoods. That seems illegal, right?
The reality isn’t that simple.
“I think one of the issues with this entire area of law and this entire area of technology is there’s a lot going on,” Cathy Gellis, an attorney with expertise in intellectual property, copyright, and technology, told TechCrunch. “It’s very complex and there are a lot of raw feelings about what is happening, both for and against.”
Last year, in one of the first rulings of its kind, Judge William Alsup ordered Anthropic to pay a mammoth $1.5 billion copyright settlement to a group of writers whose works were used to train the company’s AI models. At face value, this seemed like a moral victory favoring authors, but Judge Alsup actually ruled that Anthropic’s AI training was lawful. What Alsup penalized Anthropic for was pirating these books from illegal online shadow libraries.
“Like any reader aspiring to be a writer, Anthropic’s LLMs trained upon works not to race ahead and replicate or supplant them — but to turn a hard corner and create something different,” the judge wrote, comparing the way an LLM ingests trillions of words to a writer’s study of literature.
Gellis thinks the ruling is more advantageous for AI companies. What’s a $1.5 billion fine to a company projecting about $200 billion in annual revenue by 2028?
“I think it is generally good news for AI training that he looked at what was going on and really sort of thought it analogous to reading a copyrighted work as opposed to copying a copyrighted work,” Gellis said. “Copyright law hinges on copying, but it doesn’t hinge on using the work or experiencing the work, consuming the work, reading the work.”
Copyright law hasn’t been updated since 1976, which means that judges have to figure out how to interpret guidelines from 50 years ago when confronting legal questions that have the potential to shape the future of the AI industry.
“Everybody is very worried right now because the law is all over the place, and it’s because of this question,” Jason Henderson, Senior Attorney and Founder of the IP & Media Practice at JWL International, told TechCrunch. “They know that the AI model has been trained on so much stuff, and the law has not really caught up to that question.”
These questions often hinge on fair use law — namely, whether use of a copyrighted work is “transformative” enough to be considered legally permissible.
Fair use is a carve out of copyright law that allows for the use of copyrighted materials without explicit permission, protecting the ability to comment and iterate on copyrighted works through criticism, parody, education, and other means. Judges consider specific factors when deciding if something is fair use, including the purpose and nature of the work, the amount used, and its impact on the market.
“Copyright is always about protecting and growing the market,” Henderson noted. “The courts are kind of all over the place in their reasoning [in AI cases]. What’s tending to win is if what you’re doing is you’re training on somebody’s property because your purpose is to directly compete, then the courts will frown on it… If what you’re doing is not going to compete, then the courts are tending to find ways that it will be okay.”
Henderson is referencing a case in which the media and technology company Thomson Reuters sued the research firm Ross Intelligence for copying its content in order to build a competing, AI-based legal platform.
“Ross’s use is not transformative because it does not have a ‘further purpose or different character’ than Thomson Reuters’s,” Judge Stephanos Bibas wrote last year.
In that case, Judge Bibas decided that it was not fair use to train on Reuters’ content to make a new platform that would directly compete with it. While authors could potentially argue that chatbots are competing with them by using their works to generate new, synthetic books, that argument has not yet prevailed in court.
When it comes to the relationship between AI and copyright, Gellis finds it helpful to narrow down what we’re actually talking about – the way we think about copyright in terms of AI training is quite different from how we think about copyrighting AI-generated content.
In one case, Thaler v. Perlmutter, the court ruled that if a work is 100% AI-generated, it’s not copyrightable, which opens a whole new can of worms – how can we definitively prove whether or not a work was generated using AI, and if so, how do we know what percentage of it was created or assisted with AI?
“If you write your novel in [Microsoft] Word and run spell check, we kind of feel comfortable with the idea of saying that Word does not own your novel,” Gellis said. “[AI] is forcing us to look at a whole bunch of decisions that we kind of ignored for a while.”
Most AI companies are still lodged in pending litigation over these issues, which means that we won’t have a definitive solution to these problems any time soon.
“What you are seeing is that the initial opening volleys are being influential, and that influence itself could be undone if other courts decide different things, and it’ll take later states of litigation to figure out which one will prevail,” Gellis said. “But in the meantime, all these decisions are shaping everything that’s happening. It would be kind of foolish for the AI companies to ignore them.”

“Copyright is always about protecting and growing the market,” Henderson noted. “The courts are kind of all over the place in their reasoning [in AI cases]. What’s tending to win is if what you’re doing is you’re training on somebody’s property because your purpose is to directly compete, then the courts will frown on it… If what you’re doing is not going to compete, then the courts are tending to find ways that it will be okay.”
Henderson is referencing a case in which the media and technology company Thomson Reuters sued the research firm Ross Intelligence for copying its content in order to build a competing, AI-based legal platform.
قاضی استفانوس بیباس سال گذشته نوشت: «استفاده از راس دگرگون کننده نیست زیرا «هدف بیشتر یا شخصیت متفاوتی» نسبت به تامسون رویترز ندارد.
در آن مورد، قاضی بیباس تصمیم گرفت که استفاده منصفانه از آموزش بر روی محتوای رویترز برای ساختن پلتفرم جدیدی که مستقیماً با آن رقابت کند، نیست. در حالی که نویسندگان به طور بالقوه می‌توانند استدلال کنند که چت‌بات‌ها با استفاده از آثارشان برای تولید کتاب‌های مصنوعی جدید با آنها رقابت می‌کنند، این استدلال هنوز در دادگاه غالب نشده است.
وقتی صحبت از رابطه بین هوش مصنوعی و حق چاپ به میان می آید، گلیس این را مفید می داند که آنچه را که واقعاً در مورد آن صحبت می کنیم، محدود کنیم – طرز فکر ما در مورد حق چاپ از نظر آموزش هوش مصنوعی با طرز فکر ما در مورد حق چاپ محتوای تولید شده توسط هوش مصنوعی کاملاً متفاوت است.
در یک مورد، Thaler v. Perlmutter، دادگاه حکم داد که اگر اثری 100% با هوش مصنوعی تولید شده باشد، دارای حق نسخه‌برداری نیست، که یک قوطی کاملاً جدید از کرم‌ها را باز می‌کند – چگونه می‌توانیم به طور قطع ثابت کنیم که آیا یک اثر با استفاده از هوش مصنوعی ساخته شده است یا نه، و اگر چنین است، چگونه می‌توانیم بدانیم چند درصد از آن ساخته شده یا با هوش مصنوعی کمک شده است؟
گلیس گفت: «اگر رمان خود را در [مایکروسافت] ورد بنویسید و غلط املایی را اجرا کنید، احساس راحتی می کنیم که بگوییم ورد مالک رمان شما نیست. [هوش مصنوعی] ما را مجبور می‌کند به مجموعه‌ای از تصمیم‌هایی که برای مدتی نادیده گرفته‌ایم نگاه کنیم.»
اکثر شرکت‌های هوش مصنوعی هنوز در حال رسیدگی به این مسائل هستند، به این معنی که ما به این زودی راه حل قطعی برای این مشکلات نخواهیم داشت.
گلیس گفت: «آنچه می‌بینید این است که رگبارهای آغازین اولیه تأثیرگذار هستند، و اگر دادگاه‌های دیگر درباره چیزهای متفاوتی تصمیم بگیرند، این تأثیر می‌تواند خنثی شود، و تشخیص اینکه کدام یک پیروز خواهد شد، به مراحل بعدی دعوی نیاز دارد.» "اما در این میان، همه این تصمیمات همه چیز را شکل می دهند. نادیده گرفتن آنها برای شرکت های هوش مصنوعی احمقانه است."

title_en: We’re All Going to the World’s Fair is an intimate coming-of-age horror film
title_fa: ما همه به نمایشگاه جهانی می رویم یک فیلم ترسناک صمیمی در دوران بلوغ است
excerpt_en: Jane Schoenbrun's latest film, Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma, is making a splash in theaters right now. So it seems like the perfect time to revisit their first film, We're All Going to the World's Fair. I fell in love with this film when I first saw it at Sundance in...
excerpt_fa: جدیدترین فیلم جین شوئنبرون، جنسیت نوجوان و مرگ در کمپ میاسما، در حال حاضر در سینماها سروصدا کرده است. بنابراین به نظر می رسد زمان مناسبی برای بازدید مجدد از اولین فیلم آنها، ما همه به نمایشگاه جهانی می رویم. من وقتی این فیلم را برای اولین بار در ساندنس دیدم عاشق آن شدم...
content_en:
Jane Schoenbrun’s latest film, Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma, is making a splash in theaters right now. So it seems like the perfect time to revisit their first film, We’re All Going to the World’s Fair. I fell in love with this film when I first saw it at Sundance in 2021.
We’re All Going to the World’s Fair is an intimate coming-of-age horror film
With Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma out in theaters, now is the perfect time to revisit Jane Schoenbrun’s first film.
We are immediately introduced to our protagonist, Casey, as she engages in the World’s Fair Challenge, a sort of ARG creepypasta meets ice bucket challenge. There’s a creepy mantra, some bloodletting, and a mysterious video — basically a speedrun of horror movie tropes. But having them all delivered by this young girl alone in her room who just stares directly into her webcam the whole time is unsettling. And I actually physically recoiled when she jabbed herself repeatedly with a pin to draw blood.
The idea is that people perform the ritual and then they’re supposed to change in some sort of nebulous way. It’s set up as some sort of “game” where people are supposed to report their symptoms, as they turn into plastic or their guts and become Tetris pieces.
Ultimately, World’s Fair is a coming-of-age story about a lonely young girl. She’s never shown talking to kids her own age. Her father is never seen, only heard, and does nothing but yell. She desperately attempts to connect with others by uploading videos documenting the changes she experiences after performing the challenge.
Importantly, unlike many other coming-of-age films, World’s Fair isn’t about Casey’s sexual awakening and avoids sexualizing her entirely. Instead, it’s about her search for belonging in an extremely online world.
Basically the only other character to get any screen time is JLB, a lonely middle-aged man who claims Casey is in danger. The relationship between JLB and Casey adds another layer of unease to the film, which already blends horror elements with uncomfortably intimate glimpses into the life of a young girl. The whole thing has a voyeuristic quality. It’s never explicitly stated, but it certainly seems like JLB is attempting to groom the vulnerable Casey.
The movie stews in its uncomfortable ambiguity. And that’s part of what makes it great. It may not reach the surreal or campy heights of I Saw the TV Glow or Camp Miasma, but it’s a rare indie cinema original that uses body horror tropes in new and interesting ways.
We’re All Going to the World’s Fair is available to stream on Criterion Channel, Kanopy, and Hoopla.

جدیدترین فیلم جین شوئنبرون، جنسیت نوجوان و مرگ در کمپ میاسما، در حال حاضر در سینماها سروصدا کرده است. بنابراین به نظر می رسد زمان مناسبی برای بازدید مجدد از اولین فیلم آنها، ما همه به نمایشگاه جهانی می رویم، باشد. وقتی برای اولین بار در ساندنس در سال 2021 آن را دیدم عاشق این فیلم شدم.
ما همه به نمایشگاه جهانی می رویم یک فیلم ترسناک صمیمی در دوران بلوغ است
با اکران «سکس و مرگ نوجوانان در کمپ میاسما» در سینماها، اکنون زمان مناسبی برای بازدید مجدد از اولین فیلم جین شوئنبرون است.
ما بلافاصله با قهرمان داستان خود، کیسی، آشنا می شویم، زیرا او در چالش نمایشگاه جهانی شرکت می کند، نوعی از ARG creepypasta با چالش سطل یخ روبرو می شود. یک مانترای ترسناک، مقداری خون‌ریزی و یک ویدیوی مرموز وجود دارد - اساساً اجرای سریع فیلم‌های ترسناک. اما تحویل دادن همه آنها توسط این دختر جوان به تنهایی در اتاقش که تمام مدت مستقیماً به دوربین خود خیره شده، ناراحت کننده است. و زمانی که او بارها با سنجاق به خود ضربه زد تا خون بگیرد، من از لحاظ فیزیکی عقب نشینی کردم.
ایده این است که مردم این مراسم را انجام می دهند و سپس قرار است به نوعی تغییر کنند. این به عنوان نوعی "بازی" تنظیم شده است که در آن افراد قرار است علائم خود را گزارش کنند، زیرا آنها به پلاستیک یا روده خود تبدیل می شوند و به قطعات تتریس تبدیل می شوند.
در نهایت، نمایشگاه جهانی داستانی است در مورد یک دختر جوان تنها. او هرگز نشان داده نشده است که با بچه های هم سن خودش صحبت می کند. پدرش هرگز دیده نمی‌شود، فقط شنیده می‌شود و کاری جز فریاد زدن انجام نمی‌دهد. او ناامیدانه تلاش می‌کند تا با آپلود ویدیوهایی که تغییراتی را که پس از انجام چالش تجربه می‌کند مستند کند، با دیگران ارتباط برقرار کند.
نکته مهم این است که برخلاف بسیاری از فیلم‌های دیگر که به بلوغ می‌رسند، نمایشگاه جهانی درباره بیداری جنسی کیسی نیست و به طور کامل از جنسی کردن او اجتناب می‌کند. در عوض، این در مورد جستجوی او برای تعلق در یک دنیای بسیار آنلاین است.
اساساً تنها شخصیت دیگری که زمان زیادی برای نمایش می‌گذارد، JLB است، مردی میانسال و تنها که ادعا می‌کند کیسی در خطر است. رابطه بین JLB و کیسی لایه دیگری از ناراحتی را به فیلم اضافه می کند، که در حال حاضر عناصر ترسناک را با نگاه های ناخوشایند صمیمی به زندگی یک دختر جوان ترکیب می کند. همه چیز کیفیت فضولی دارد. این هرگز به صراحت بیان نشده است، اما مطمئناً به نظر می رسد که JLB در تلاش است تا کیسی آسیب پذیر را اصلاح کند.
فیلم در ابهام ناخوشایند خود غرق می شود. و این بخشی از چیزی است که آن را عالی می کند. ممکن است به اوج‌های سورئال یا کمپینگ I Saw the TV Glow یا Camp Miasma نرسد، اما یک سینمای مستقل کمیاب است که از سبک‌های ترسناک بدن به روش‌های جدید و جالبی استفاده می‌کند.
ما همه به نمایشگاه جهانی می رویم برای پخش در Criterion Channel، Kanopy و Hoopla در دسترس است.
